To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we present a novel end to end conditional Imitation Learning approach, that combines both lateral and longitudinal controls on a real vehicle.
we propose a method to learn to drive a vehicle in a real world urban setting, using a combination of lateral and longitudinal control, by imitating the behaviour of a human driver.
we present a conditional imitation learning approach for driving in urban streets with traffic, and that our method is able to drive 35km of new routes in urban streets, which we believe is a first.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a robust, scalable and safe system for urban driving, with a focus on learning from human driving demonstrations, rather than hand crafting decision rules.
learning representations and policies for autonomous urban driving.
the problem of imitation learning from human driving demonstrations in urban environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we are the first to demonstrate end to end IL for urban autonomous driving in a real vehicle.
we have demonstrated that it is possible to learn a driving policy for an autonomous vehicle in a complex real world environment, using imitation learning from human demonstrations.
we present the first end to end conditional IL for urban autonomous driving on a real vehicle, with a large scale dataset, in a complex real world environment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present an approach to learn a policy from human demonstrations for autonomous driving in urban environments.
our approach is the first end to end imitation learning system to drive a real vehicle in urban environments.
we present the first end to end conditional IL system for autonomous driving, with a focus on real world urban driving, that is robust to dataset bias and that is evaluated in the real world.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL is feasible for urban autonomous driving in real world traffic.
imitation learning is a viable approach to learn driving policies for autonomous vehicles in complex urban scenarios, with a limited amount of data.

we can learn generalised driving behaviour from human driving demonstrations, which can be used to follow a route in urban driving with simple traffic, without the need for hand crafting complex decision making rules.
